messages.text: Can you look at the screenshot I sent? The page keeps kicking me back to the sign-in screen.
Send me the code it texts you, then leave it open. I can reset it before my 9.
Also the form wants the two readings from last week and the lab packet number.
Got it. Put the cuff notebook and the yellow packet by the laptop and I'll fill in the fields tonight.
Lunch after the pipeline review or are you doing the desk-salad thing again?
Desk salad. I looked at February last night and the card line was $5,600, so I am behaving for a bit.
That explains the heroic grocery-store container. Was that from the new trail shoes and the frame shop run?
If you actually go to that coffee thing tonight, do not open with Salesforce dashboards.
Those, plus two sit-down checks I forgot were both on the same statement.
Noted. One beverage, one hour, no pipeline talk unless she asks.
Good. Also leave yourself time after. You always book these right before going back to your quiet apartment and overthinking.
That's why the calendar says walk home by the river after. Easier reset than scrolling on the couch.
Forecast call moved to 4:10. Also Priya asked if you and Evan are still in for Seventh Son after the quiz sheets.
Yep. I can make it if we keep the post-round food close by. Tell Priya I still owe her from the OSU bracket argument.
Noted. I am leaving after round 3 unless you start re-checking Salesforce at the table.
Fair. I will close the laptop before I walk over.
You still staring at the forecast tab? Your replies got very clipped after the 4 pm call.
Yeah. Almost typed a messy thing into the feed and deleted it. Can I send you the version with names removed?
Send it. Then close Salesforce and go get shots up or grab one of your Cavs people.
Marcus is around later. I'll text him after I clean this up.
You still have that old picture from the Statehouse steps? The one where we left before it got loud.
Yeah, buried in my 2020 folder. I remember us walking maybe an hour, then me sending a little to that legal-help fund afterward.
That was the same week I told you about the stop on Morse Rd, right?
I think so. That conversation stayed with me more than the signs did.
When you come Sunday, can you carry down the blue school tote from the Worthington house boxes? It has your old Cardinal papers and Gina's class photos.
Yep. Is that also where you kept the Riverside envelope?
I think so, beside my teaching certificates and your dad's business folder. Please don't let him reorganize it first.
I found the card from your first week there in the kitchen drawer. March again already.
That drawer is a time capsule. I need that first-week energy for the packet Leah and I are polishing.
Bring it Sunday and I will look for typos. Are you still adding the page about handling a bigger territory?
Yes. Also a short section on the stuff I have learned since they gave me people to coach.
I found your old Calvino paperback in the dining room stack. Do you want it back for your shelf?
I found the little black notebook from when we used to keep you busy in those long lobby lines.
Yes, please. I made room next to the little board and the bag of jumper wires on the side table.
The one with the crooked dinosaurs and music-note borders?
Yes. I tucked it by the piano bench so you can laugh at it Sunday.
I will bring it Sunday. And do not leave wires near the sauce pan again.
Do not let Dad throw that in the recycling pile.
Fair. The pan is back in the cabinet and the wires are clipped together.
Can you look at this portal thing before Maria's 10:40 appointment? It keeps telling me the password is wrong.
Forward me the screenshot. I can reset it before my 9:30 call, then swing by if it still acts up.
Sent it. Gina said she can cover the pharmacy stop, so just the login and forms if you have time.
Got it. I'll print the two pages and leave them on the kitchen table.
Browns group is coming Sunday. I have 2 six-packs and those porch cigars Jim likes. Need anything else?
I'm good with one beer after dinner. Please keep the porch stuff outside; my jacket still smelled like Jim's garage last time.
Noted. Your mother is making extra sausage bread too.
That is the real danger. I already bought pretzels for later because forecast cleanup is going sideways.
I found the blue hymnal from St. Agatha's in the closet. The one with your grandmother's card tucked inside.
Do not toss that. I still remember the organ starting before the candles came down the aisle.
I would never toss it. Easter morning will sound strange without you humming along.
Put me down for Easter with you. I am not promising every Sunday, but that one I can do.
Saw that rate article. Still think you keep renting until the numbers stop looking dumb.
Yeah. I split the bonus instead of letting it sit in checking: house bucket, boring cushion, and the California folder.
Good. Don't let a hotel website talk you into using the card.
That's why I moved it before dinner. If it stays visible, I start justifying things.
I sent the forecast note early. You can ignore it until your 8:00 wall comes down.
Good. Charger is on the dresser and the sales apps are still asleep.
Then do your lap and come back after coffee. Nothing burns down before 8.
Finance kicked back my March tracker again. Did your worksheet split regular money from the accelerator tab?
Your 2:00 deck still has the old implementation slide. Want me to send the one I used with Priya yesterday?
Are you eating the sad desk sandwich again or did Sunday John come through?
Yeah. Regular lines are the 15th and 31st. The extra tab says monthly unless they roll it into the quarter review.
Yes please. Nina is joining for the product translation part, and I need Jamal's two openers to stop promising the moon in discovery.
Sunday John came through. Container has chicken, zucchini, a scoop of farro, and enough sauce to survive the forecast meeting.
Same here. Also People Ops wants the team-lead attestations by 4, so do that before Salesforce eats your afternoon.
Good. Bring whatever bottle you were bragging about if we do dinner after close.
Sending. Also, your stage-3 totals jumped because Ross left three close dates blank again.
Already open. Feb export still shows 10,800 before all the deductions, so I am copying the numbers carefully.
The Zin is still unopened. It needs food, not a paper cup by my laptop.
I saw it. I'm fixing the sheet before the readout so nobody treats that number like reality.
Are you still leaving by 5:20, or did Forecastzilla win?
Leaving. I already moved the short garage set to lunch, so the evening court slot is staying put.
Good. Yesterday you were one Salesforce refresh away from biting someone.
Exactly why I'm not giving the shoes back to the trunk gods tonight.
Please tell me you closed the laptop after the forecast call.
Almost. Neck is doing that concrete-block thing, so I am forcing dinner and a page in the notebook before I look again.
You still at the office or did you escape after forecast cleanup?
Still here. Third badge swipe this week and I promised myself I would leave by 5:30.
Good. Also your 2pm with Dr. R is on your calendar Tuesday, right? Do not let Salesforce eat that slot.
It is blocked. I already moved the pipeline review around it.
Do not start checking Salesforce from the parking lot. Also use the sick hours if your voice is still rough Monday.
Fair. I already put Monday morning as remote unless the new rep needs me in the room.
You still coming Sunday? Also saw your note about the city packet.
Yeah, 10 at the rec. And I kept thinking about what you said after that traffic thing on Cleveland Ave.
Good. Just remember your two warning-and-go stories are not the whole movie.
Exactly. Mine were license, insurance, awkward small talk, done. That is why I am trying to read the tables before I open my mouth.
That jacket you ordered, porch delivery or one of those lockers?
Locker by the High St shops. Easier to grab after I hit the library.
Good. You still getting over to that park nearby before work gets loud?
Yeah, short lap tomorrow morning, then coffee and back before calls.
Coffee after pickup tomorrow or you doing your envelope ritual again?
Coffee works. I already grabbed the BOE envelope and I'm down to the school board and auditor lines.
Send me the two links you trusted. My aunt is asking and Facebook is useless.
I'll send the League sheet and the Dispatch rundown. For the auditor race I'm checking each campaign page too.
I found a red folder in the closet with your old Buckeye card and a printout from Fisher. Do you still need those papers?
Yes, please keep it out. The HR form wants the old PDF with the database/accounting coursework listed.
There are no newer campus papers in here, just the Columbus ones from before you started working full time.
That is the right stack. I only need that one and nothing from any officer paperwork pile Dad keeps.
That Columbia Gas notice you showed me, does it match what they pulled last month?
Pretty close. Electric was higher too, probably the drafty windows on the north wall again.
Ask the building guy to seal it. Older brick places lose heat around those frames.
I put in the ticket. He has to buzz from the front because Gina still has my spare key.
The accountant wants my 1099s. Do you have to send the same pile?
Pretty much: W-2, bank interest, brokerage dividends. Nothing from the state showed up for me this year.
Good. And if your tires are as bald as you said, don't wait until the cord is showing.
I priced it at $412 installed. Annoying, but checking plus the online account can handle it without touching rent.
Can you look at this MyChart thing Sunday? Mine has three pages and yours probably has two.
Sure. Mine was quick last week: work card, HSA swipe, update the empty bottle section, then out.
Ask your doctor about those spring shots too. I keep seeing different TV answers.
I already saved the CDC page and Dr. N. pointed me to the OSU Wexner chart. I'll print both for you.
Good run today. You good after that last call you mentioned?
Better after sweating. Driving past three packed driveways with everyone doing dinner made the apartment sound rough in advance.
Come over for the second half if you want. I got coffee too, even if it is the lazy pod kind.
On my way. No need for a big talk, just don't let me check work email during commercials.
For the church cookbook page, use your great-grandmother Lucia's pizzelle note, not my version. Hers has the orange zest.
Got it. Also, is it 'grazie mille' or am I making that up?
That one is right. Do not get fancy past that or Aunt Rose will correct you at dinner.
Fair. I will stick to the two words and the cookie recipe.
I made extra sauce if you want to stop by after work tomorrow.
Yes please. I just added up Kroger and the two lunches from last week and homemade dinner sounds smarter.
Good. Bring containers. Your father also said not to forget that portal payment clears early this week.
Already scheduled. That $1,450 hits Wednesday, so free sauce is excellent timing.
You still doing that spreadsheet lunch break thing or did Salesforce finally win?
Spreadsheet wins. I matched the Chase points categories, moved the statement amount to autopay, and checked the $17k federal line.
That is very you. Did you ever tour that Clintonville place?
Skipped it after the calculator spit out the monthly number. My lease renewal looks boring, which is kind of the point right now.
When you come Sunday, can you bring the little level? Your father moved the hallway shelf again.
Yep. I need it anyway for the new 16x20 over my desk.
The one you showed me after that High Street stop? Use two hooks this time, please.
I learned from the crooked couch wall situation. Two hooks.
Saw a condo listing near you. Two bedrooms. Rate is ugly but the monthly is not insane if you keep renting a year.
Send it. I still like my place, even if the second bedroom idea is more 'maybe someday' than actual plan.
You do not need to buy for an imaginary future. Just know the numbers.
Exactly. I can picture a bigger setup later, but I am not making a spreadsheet around someone I have not met.
You still staring at Salesforce or did you actually shut the laptop?
Closed it. Bowl of pasta, couch, one episode, then checking the score if Cleveland keeps it close.
Good. No dashboard tabs during dinner.
Deal. Marcus already sent three texts about the fourth quarter like I control the rotations.
You in tonight? We're at 7 and nobody wants to run with uneven teams again.
I'm in. Need ten minutes at home first for the band and heel raises.
Good. Bring the white shirt. And don't skip the brace like last time.
Packed already. If I bail, roast me in the thread.
I found the little Santa Fe church brochure you left in my cookbook. Was that from the trip with the red rocks?
Yep. Same folder as the canyon photos. That was one of the better four-day stretches I took last year.
You always come back with rocks, ticket stubs, and too many photos of old doorways.
That is basically the winning formula.
Found the old insurance claim from your Civic. Was that the same year someone smashed the window downtown?
Different car. I called the non-emergency number from the lot, waited around, then mostly handled glass and insurance.
I remember you being more annoyed about the hold music than the report.
Pretty much. That is part of why the council notes about response triage and follow-up logs caught my eye.
Your mother says the St. John's booth list is starting already. I told her you can do tickets after work if the sales people let you breathe.
Tickets are fine. I just need the exact night so I can block it before quarter-end eats my calendar.
She has cousins texting her from three directions. Same crew as last year, plus Gina if Luca's game ends early.
Sounds right. Put me wherever Mom needs me, just not next to Uncle Dom if he's comparing parking prices again.
Tax folder question. Do you need more than that W-2 from your company or is that it?
That should be it for wages. I will bring the PDF Sunday and check the health plan forms too.
Good. Your mother also wants you to look at her dental login while you are here.
I can do both after dinner, before I start the Sunday night quote cleanup.
Mom asked if you want containers back or if she can keep the square ones.
Tell her to keep two. I froze the little potato pillows in the round ones and I need room for sauce.
Luca says your freezer is just dumplings and basketball ice packs.
Mostly accurate. I also hid a Barolo behind the seltzer so I don't open it on a random Thursday.
Mom says the blue exercise strap is missing and Dad says the TV app updated itself, which sounds like a trap.
Dad says the mailer with the giant red font is garbage. Can you look before Sunday dinner?
Yep. Tell him not to toss it yet. I'll compare it with the county sample and the candidate sites.
I'll swing by after work tomorrow. I can pair the remote again and check the message Dad printed.
Thank you. I can call Mom after dinner and do the feelings part while you do the blinking-screen part.
Also Mom asked if you're bringing your blue pen like every November.
Deal. Ask her if she needs the shower chair moved back before Saturday.
Only if Luca promises not to turn it into a soccer-field map again.
Jamal said thanks for actually listening yesterday instead of doing the manager nod.
He told me about the lane-change stop after the client dinner. I kept thinking about how routine he made it sound.
Also, your lunch spreadsheet has clinic-call hours, school board dates, and that power-plant comment deadline. Very on-brand for you.
Trying to keep the little tasks from getting lost behind forecast chaos.
Are you going straight to the annex tonight or stopping home first?
Straight there. Week 3 starts at 6:30 and I do not trust 315 after 5.
Good. Evan said he and Priya are looking at the CMA late hours next Friday if you want in.
That works. I will ask them whether we are doing the cafe there or somewhere in Bexley after.
You still making 7 on Sunday or are you trapped in laptop jail again?
I'll make it. Just finished listening to three Gong calls and I have two one-on-ones left to prep.
That sounds like punishment with headphones.
Only when the notes say 'verbal yes' and the actual call says 'maybe after budget review.' Big difference.
You making Cavs tipoff or still wandering around Clintonville?
On High now. Did the Park of Roses loop after dinner at Harvest.
That is a very you pre-game. Coffee tomorrow after pickup?
Yep. Cup O Joe works, then I can hop downtown from there.
Are you still putting the phone out by the dresser at night?
Yes. Notebook is on the nightstand, lights at 10:30 tonight.
Good. Eat something real tomorrow before you start answering everybody.
Plan is coffee, a few quiet minutes, then the block.
Found an old benefits form. It asks for your date as 08/22/89 and I don't want to fat-finger it.
That's right. Leave the hospital line blank if it isn't already typed.
Typed says Riverside. Also found the old HVAC distributor badge from my operations desk if your mother wants it in the folder.
Put it with the business degree copy so it doesn't get lost.
When you fill out that new-patient packet for Mom, same as mine: Columbus for both of us, Worthington address back then.
Thanks. Mine is the Riverside copy from '89, right?
Yes. And on those background boxes, you know what we usually mark. The separate origin one is no.
Perfect. I will keep it consistent with the last insurance forms.
Mom says if you still have her blue program from the orchestra hall, bring it Sunday.
The folded one with my marker scribbles on the back?
Probably. She keeps describing it like it belongs in the family archive.
Tell her I found it between old Cavs ticket stubs.
Lunch moved to 12:45. I need ten minutes to fix my expense report before finance yells.
Works. I was using the extra time to finish my March spreadsheet anyway.
The one with the color-coded tabs?
Yep. It has March at $1,550 set aside after bills if commissions land like forecast, and all income lines are just work, interest, and dividends.
Did compliance accept your education page yet, or are they still making everyone retype ancient details?
Still retyping. I had to list the Fisher undergrad record, plus the systems analysis and database courses they asked about.
Your slide 6 is stronger if you lead with the 2024 handoff. Two cycles of keeping that crew steady matters.
For the other boxes, leave them empty if they don't apply. Don't overthink it.
Good call. I was burying it under the March 2022 ramp story.
Done. No current program number, no later diploma upload, and nothing for the service-document line.
Also, stop calling the Midwest map a someday thing. Put the number beside it and make them react.
I added the number. Saved the tiny-firm idea for the last page so it does not sound like I am half out the door.
Did the tiny blinking thing survive your Salesforce rage-clean?
Barely. It is sitting under the framed Blue Jackets print with a note that says do not unplug.
That sounds like your living room has a lab bench disguised as decor.
Decor is generous. I found the fix in a forum reply from 2019 and called it a night.
Did you eat before your appointment, honey? Those morning slots always run late.
I did. It was easy: no bottle names to type, paid the $25 with the HSA card, and grabbed lunch after.
Good. Your father would have argued with the tablet for ten minutes.
The nurse also said Dr. N.'s shot note matches the hospital page, so I stopped second-guessing it.
When you come Sunday, can you look at my portal? Also, do your work statements show any dues line? Mine used to.
Sure. Mine just has taxes, 401k, HSA, insurance, the usual stuff. No dues line.
Makes sense. Bring the laptop. Your mother says pasta at 5.
Will do. First March deposit hits Monday, so I am checking the deductions anyway.
Your mother asked if you want us to order from Moretti's tomorrow or just eat here.
Eat there if that's okay. I am keeping March quieter after those shoes and the print.
Makes sense. Bring the receipt if you want me to look at the return policy on the shoes.
Keeping them. Just skipping the extra stuff this month, including the button-downs I had open in my cart.
Mom moved sauce to 1:30. Luca wants to know if Uncle John is bringing the green ball.
I can. Highbanks crew is doing the north loop at 10, so I may show up with muddy shoes.
Fine, but bag them before Mom sees the kitchen. Also yes, go do the loop. You text nicer after.
Luca found the volcano kit box in your trunk last time and has been asking if Uncle John is doing 'explosions' again.
Tell him I upgraded to something less messy. Also, is Mark still bringing him by Mom and Dad's around 4?
Yep. Mark has him after soccer, then we're all heading over. Mom said bring your laptop because Dad's bill site is being weird.
Perfect. I'll bring the kit and handle the bill site before dinner.
Coffee after pickup or are you pretending to be responsible today?
Coffee yes, diner no. My food column is already at $512 and we still have Russo's Friday.
One biscuit sandwich didn't ruin America but fine. Stauf's then.
Deal. I am trying to keep the whole March sheet under 5,000 for once.
I can bring wings tonight if your place is still the move.
Yeah. I made rice and cleaned enough of the living room to pretend I have standards.
Tipoff at 8. Do not let me sit under that lamp again.
Lamp moved. If they start ugly, we switch to the last episode I was saving after work.
Cavs at my place tonight. Dave brought those little squares again if you want one.
I'll pass on the square. Last time I got quiet and watched everyone from inside my own skull.
Fair. I'll grab wings. You bringing anything?
Pretzels and a tallboy. Keeping it boring after this week.
Luca asked if Uncle John is coming for pasta or if he is choosing tall-guy ball again.
Tell him tall-guy ball won today. I may swing by after, but if everyone is deep into bedtime mode I won't interrupt.
You're not interrupting. Also call or text someone before you sit there refreshing work stuff all night.
Marcus said coffee after the run. I'll do that first, then maybe stop by for leftovers.
You alive after those hills yesterday or am I carrying us at pickup?
Calves are annoyed, but I am functional. Weather held, so the Worthington crew pushed the longer loop.
Of course you found stairs in the woods and called it relaxing.
Only because there was a small town diner after. Balance.
I started the sauce before church. If you come by later, I made the long noodles you liked when you were little.
I'll be there after pickup. Save me the corner piece if you make the baked tray too.
Already done. Your aunt called twice about whether the cousins are coming, so bring patience.
Your father said the apartment office slipped another envelope under your door. Is everything okay?
Just renewal papers. I am comparing that with the Powell listing Dad sent, but the rate quote made my eyes hurt.
Come for pasta and bring the papers if you want another set of eyes.
I will. I also want Dad to sanity-check the Honda payoff screen; it is still around $8k after this month's draft.
Your mother said you knew the old responses better than the people who show up every week.
Muscle memory. I mostly followed the organ and tried not to mess up the kneeling timing.
She liked having you there. Also remind me how to print that insurance form tonight.
I will come by after work. And yes, I caught her smiling when the choir did the old Marian song.
Luca asked why Uncle John has that giant ice pack in his freezer.
Tessa asked if you are still up for trivia Friday. I told her your only hard stop is not missing Cavs tipoff.
Tell him it's the glamorous Tuesday-night recovery plan.
Trivia is fine. Low stakes. Tell her I am not promising charm after round three.
As long as Marcus keeps getting you out of the house, I'll allow the freezer clutter.
Fair. Also Mom asked if you want leftovers Sunday or if your fridge is doing that bachelor-apartment echo again.
Leftovers yes. And tell Mom the fridge has yogurt, eggs, and one heroic bag of spinach.
Are you eating real dinner tonight or just coffee and crackers again?
Real dinner. I did the ten-minute mat thing first because my shoulders were up by my ears.
Good. Put the phone away after and write it out like you said. You sleep better when you do that.
Notebook is already on the table. No more dashboard tonight.
Luca says if you drive near cliffs you have to send a picture of every tunnel. His rule, not mine.
Mom found the picture of us on the Linworth porch. You look sixteen and annoyed, I look tiny and smug.
Tell him I have to earn the tunnel pictures first. I hid the motel tab behind the bank tab tonight.
That was probably before my Thomas Worthington bus came. Please tell me Dad's shorts did not make the photo.
Very mature. Also please keep the grown-up piles funded so Mom doesn't hear you sold a kidney for a view.
They did. Also Mom tucked her reading-room badge behind it, because apparently every memory needs a file system.
House pile and boring pile both got fed. The view pile can wait its turn.
Honey, the little envelope from the plan came today. Your father put it by the fruit bowl so he doesn't lose it.
I'll read it Sunday and compare it with the PDF he sent me.
Could you also show me why my phone won't open the video from Luca? It just spins.
Yes. And save your exercise sheet for me so I can take a picture before it gets sauce on it.
Do you want me to send lasagna home Sunday or are you cooking after work?
Send some if there is extra. My little freezer is already packed but I can make room.
I also found your water bill from last year in the folder here. Do you need it for taxes?
Yes, please put it with the insurance stuff. I keep all the apartment receipts in one folder now.
That little controller you showed me, does it need a special power cord or just the same phone charger?
Phone charger works. Mine is on the desk by the cookbooks if you want to see the plug Sunday.
Bring the one with the red light. I want to understand why it keeps counting wrong.
I will. Someone online had the same counter issue, so I marked the wiring change with tape.
Luca says your apartment has 'museum walls' because everything is straight and serious.
Tell him the crooked one by the record shelf is still under review.
Also he wants to know if the red-and-black one came from the place with the giant stairs downtown.
Different stop. That one was after the Friday opening in Franklinton.
Luca wants you to say the toast at Dad's birthday because he thinks you sound 'official.'
He is confusing official with me knowing exactly three dinner words.
Three is generous. Just do the Grandpa Tony line about everybody being born around Columbus and then say the food word Mom likes.
Deal. Local-history speech plus one borrowed phrase.
Mom asked why you had three tabs open at dinner: school levy, river cleanup, and some poll-worker thing. I said that is just John with lasagna.
I was also trying to find the receipt from the Columbus fund I sent to after that 2020 walk. Dad's scanner was right there.
Luca still remembers you explaining why people were carrying water bottles and phone chargers.
Mostly I remember Marcus talking afterward and me realizing I had been guessing too much from a distance.
You still awake or did Salesforce finally release you?
Awake. One glass of red, half a bag of chips, and now I am forty tabs deep in dumb reels.
Close the laptop and the tabs. Also Luca says you owe him soccer on Sunday.
Tell him yes. And no, I am not touching the party gummies from your neighbor's cooler tomorrow.
Coffee after pickup or you bouncing?
I can hang but probably just coffee, not diner. March has been repair work after that $5,600 February.
The February with the new hiking kicks and the wall thing?
Yep. And I still have that jacket tab open, so diner pancakes can wait.
Coffee after run? You looked like you had spreadsheets in your head during pickup.
Yeah. I am trying to turn four Marches of receipts into a clean ask.
Ask for the bigger map, not another badge. You already survived two years of other people's quotas landing on your phone.
That is the pitch. Bigger map now, higher table later, then someday my own little shop.
Mom is already asking who is riding with who for Easter. Luca wants to sit by you because you know when the bells happen.
Tell him the bells are the easy part. The hard part is staying quiet during the incense cloud.
You laugh, but you still get weirdly focused when the choir starts.
That room has a sound I grew up with. I can do Easter morning, then I have to duck out before the egg chaos.
Luca's school form asks if his emergency contact has any court dates or case numbers. You are still the easy uncle, right?
Still boring on that front. Closest paperwork is the downtown window smash and two roadside warnings.
Boring is useful. Also Mom said you were doing another city comment thing?
Just editing it. Trying to keep my own smooth experiences from sounding like the default setting for everyone.
You still want the school levy spreadsheet from my neighbor? She's obsessive but usually right.
Yes please. I'm trying to lock my card before quarter-end swallows my brain.
Figured. Also the downtown council forum clip you sent was very you: practical housing answer gets your checkmark, culture-war monologue gets deleted.
Pretty much. I can handle boring and competent. I don't have patience for the cable-news audition.
Same time tonight. I told Darnell you'd cover him if his shift runs late.
Yeah, I'll be there. Calendar already blocked.
Left side holding up after last week?
Fine if I do the warmup and don't pretend I'm 22.
CHC still has eight for Thursday. You in or are the spreadsheet people holding you hostage?
In. Missed Sunday walk and Monday bands, so I'm not skipping another one.
Yeah, I could tell. You were answering texts like every message owed you money.
Thursday fixes that. Save me a spot before the tall guy claims permanent corner rights.
You watching Cavs or did I miss the window? Long day with the regional deck.
Third quarter. Come through or call me. Your choice.
Calling. I deleted the half-written post and put shoes by the door for tomorrow morning instead.
Good. Five minutes on the deck, then we talk Garland missing bunnies.
Luca tried calling you before school, but I told him Uncle John does not touch the dresser phone before 8.
Ha. Accurate. I am doing the notebook and a no-earbuds loop first.
Perfect. Text him after the lap and he can tell you about the science kit disaster.
Can you bring Luca's library book Sunday? He left it in your car.
Yep, I'm returning mine tonight anyway. Going past the lockers and then cutting up High.
Of course you have a whole route. Are you doing your Whetstone loop too?
Short one. Then maybe Northstar if it is not packed.
Your two-person scene with the imaginary copier was better than it had any right to be.
I blame the quarter-end printer trauma. Same time next Thursday for week 5?
Yep. Also Priya sent the Franklinton opening details for Saturday. Evan is pushing for Little Palace after.
I am in. I will text them once I get home.
Can you stop by Sunday and look at that portal password? Also, your mother says you sounded wiped out.
Yes. Rough close week. Woke up with the band-around-the-forehead thing again, so I am doing notes before work and skipping the extra coffee.
Good. One thing at a time. Do you still have that standing call after this quarter ends?
Yes, next one is already blocked for April. It helps me keep the spillover off the team.
Your mother said you needed the file box. I see BuckeyeLink, Fisher, and the old tuition receipts. Anything from my VA envelope?
No, leave your envelope alone. Mine is just the Columbus transcript and the HR checklist.
The checklist has blank spots for current campus ID, later diploma, and DD-214. You sure that's right?
Yes. The only attachment they need from me is the old Fisher PDF with the tech-business courses.
I looked at that house link again. Numbers don't mean much if the listing hides the roof age.
Exactly. Same thing at work today. Seven people rolled into my sheet and three tiny missing fields changed the whole Friday readout.
Then make them fill the boxes before anyone argues about the total.
That's the plan. Then I have a Zoom Monday with the two front-end folks and Nina to tighten the handoff language.
Dad is asking if you can sanity-check his insurance thing Sunday. Also Luca wants to know if rich Uncle John is buying the big science kit.
